## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sekkhattika* is a canonical Abhidhamma text located in the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh treatise of the Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka, cataloged as Patthana 13.11 [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. It investigates conditional relations in terms of the triad (*tika*) concerning trainees (*sekha*), beyond-training (*asekha*), and neither. The text has received no distinct modern translations or individual critical treatments within the secondary literature cited in the dossier [SuttaCentral].

According to computational analysis by DharmaNexus, the text exhibits 573 textual reuse matches across 82 other Pali canonical texts, reflecting the highly systematic and combinatorial character of the *Paṭṭhāna* [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive overlap is with *Sekkhattika* of the first division (Patthana 1.12), sharing 110 passages (over 20,000 characters), including the alignment of §3.1_0–5.1_0 with §57.1–59.1_1 [DharmaNexus]. It also shares significant formulaic phrasing with contiguous sections of the thirteenth division, including the *Parittattika* (Patthana 13.12), *Saṁkiliṭṭhattika* (Patthana 13.5), and *Vipākattika* (Patthana 13.3), as well as cross-combinations like the *Tika Kusalattika* (Patthana 5.2) and *Tika Hetuduka* (Patthana 4.1) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matching, DharmaNexus detects minor alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *Abhidharmakośaśāstrakārikābhāṣya* (D4091), though no formal parallel is identified by SuttaCentral [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral].
